host_memory_diagnostic.limits: mallinfo2 and malloc_info describe glibc arenas and direct mmap allocations known to glibc, not all TensorFlow/CUDA/custom native allocators. Free malloc arena space is not necessarily fully resident or fully releasable. Only smaps RSS before/after trim measures observed resident return. malloc_trim success alone does not measure bytes.

limits: Five saved historical rounds constitute finite lifecycle replay, not fresh on-policy learning or strength evidence.
No new workers or games were launched; production worker coexistence remains untested.

Post-update host RSS rose overall across the five observations, with one declining boundary; this run did not establish a natural host-memory plateau. Dead cache tensor wrappers/readers and flat active GPU bytes alone do not identify the cause of retained host RSS.
Dead Python tensor wrappers and a flat active TF-current tail do not prove universal absence of C++ allocator retention.
NVML reservation can remain high after tensor release; sampled headroom can miss shorter peaks and Windows clock adjustments do not affect monotonic durations.
System OOM/swap/PSI counters can include unrelated Linux activity; Windows paging is unmeasured.
Remote source/cleanup integrity is supported by checksummed coordinator and root read-only proofs; this independent audit ran no remote command or TensorFlow.
